Read it back with list-database-extensions: a row that survives with status `failed` is the refusal, and a row that is gone is a drop the daemon accepted. The package stays installed on the server, deliberately — it is shared by every database on that daemon.

| Parameter                                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Database server uuid, from list-database-servers.                                                                                      |
| `managed_database` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The database uuid to drop it from, from list-database-extensions.                                                                      |
| `extension` <span class="req">required</span>        | string | The extension name as list-database-extensions reports it — `vector` or `postgis`. There is no cascade argument and no force argument. |
| `organization`                                       | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                      |

### `add-database-replica`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>database-servers.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Add a PostgreSQL streaming replica of a managed database server on another bootstrapped server (managed node). PostgreSQL only — other engines are refused with the reason. Queued: PostgreSQL is installed on the target exactly as a normal setup would, then its data directory is replaced by a base backup of the primary; a PostgreSQL on the target holding anything this cluster does not account for is refused, never overwritten. The primary gains a replication login (generated once, never returned), a replication slot and a firewall rule for the replica. The first replica creates the cluster and makes the named server its primary. Refused for adopted servers, for a server that is itself a replica, and for a server that is not Active. Poll get-database-cluster: the new member reads `pending`/`configuring` until the setup finishes, `failed` with its reason otherwise.

| Parameter                                           | Type   | Description                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The primary's database server uuid (or any member — the replica is added to the cluster's primary).                    |
| `node` <span class="req">required</span>            | string | Managed node uuid to put the replica on, from list-managed-nodes. Must be bootstrapped and not already carry a member. |
| `organization`                                      | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                      |

### `add-storage-member`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>storage-servers.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Add a bootstrapped server to a managed storage server's Garage cluster. Queues the setup pipeline, which installs Garage on the new node with the cluster's existing secret, opens the cluster RPC port between members only (never to the allowlist), connects it, gives it a layout role in the zone you name, and lets Garage rebalance data onto it. Every node is set up again, one at a time. Refused for adopted servers, while a setup is running, for a node without an internal IP, and for a node that already runs a storage daemon for G8Deck (one per machine). Read the result back with get-storage-cluster.

| Parameter                                          | Type   | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `storage_server` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Storage server uuid.                                                                                                                                             |
| `node` <span class="req">required</span>           | string | Managed node uuid, from list-managed-nodes. Must be bootstrapped, have an internal IP, and not already run storage.                                              |
| `zone`                                             | string | Layout zone (letters, digits, hyphens). Garage spreads copies across zones first; give nodes in different racks or data centres different zones. Default g8deck. |
| `organization`                                     | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                |

### `start-node-bootstrap`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Bootstrap a machine into an SSH-capable provider: install the baseline, configure the firewall, create the management user and rotate onto a generated key. The work is queued on the infra redis connection, supervised by Horizon. The provider must belong to your organisation and must speak SSH.

| Parameter                                    | Type    | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Provider uuid. Must belong to your organisation and speak SSH.    |
| `host` <span class="req">required</span>     | string  | Hostname or IP of the machine to bootstrap.                       |
| `user`                                       | string  | SSH login user (default root).                                    |
| `port`                                       | integer | SSH port (default 22).                                            |
| `template`                                   | string  | Bootstrap template uuid or slug. Omit to use your default.        |
| `organization`                               | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `create-cloud-server`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.create.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Create a server at the organisation's connected cloud account (DigitalOcean today) and set it up with a bootstrap template — the New Server page's action. This SPENDS MONEY at the customer's account the moment it succeeds. Refused before any spend when the plan has no room for another server, when no account is connected, or when the image is not one a visible setup template can bootstrap (the response lists the images that are). G8Deck mints the machine's SSH key; nothing secret is returned. Queued: poll get-bootstrap-job with the returned job uuid — it waits for the machine to report an address, then bootstraps.

| Parameter                                  | Type   | Description                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span>   | string | Server name and hostname: letters, numbers, dots and hyphens. Unique in the organisation.   |
| `region` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Vendor region slug, e.g. sgp1.                                                              |
| `size` <span class="req">required</span>   | string | Vendor size slug, e.g. s-1vcpu-1gb. Must be sold in the region.                             |
| `image` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Vendor image slug, e.g. ubuntu-24-04-x64. Must match a setup template's release.            |
| `template`                                 | string | Bootstrap template uuid or slug. Omit to use the first template for that exact release.     |
| `integration`                              | string | Cloud account (integration) uuid. Omit to use the organisation's connected compute account. |
| `organization`                             | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                           |

### `register-ssh-server`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.create.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Register a machine that already exists (any host reachable over SSH) and bootstrap it. Two calls: the FIRST, without `fingerprint`, records nothing and returns the SSH host key fingerprint the address presents — verify it against the machine's own console or `ssh-keygen -lf`. The SECOND repeats the same arguments plus `fingerprint`; it is compared with what the host presents, and only on a match is the server recorded with that key pinned and the bootstrap queued (poll get-bootstrap-job). Exactly one of private_key or password; both are inbound only and never returned. Refused for this G8Deck control plane's own address and for a name already used in the organisation. Re-sending a confirmed call returns the server already registered rather than a second one.

| Parameter                                | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Server name, unique in the organisation.                                                                                                                                   |
| `host` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Hostname or IP of the machine. Never this control plane.                                                                                                                   |
| `port`                                   | integer | SSH port (default 22).                                                                                                                                                     |
| `user`                                   | string  | SSH login user (default root).                                                                                                                                             |
| `hosted_at`                              | string  | Where the machine lives (default bare_metal, shown as Other). Bookkeeping: every choice is reached over SSH. One of: `do`, `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `hetzner`, `bare_metal`. |
| `private_key`                            | string  | SSH private key, inbound only. Exactly one of private_key or password.                                                                                                     |
| `password`                               | string  | SSH password, inbound only. The bootstrap rotates onto a generated key.                                                                                                    |
| `fingerprint`                            | string  | Omit on the first call. On the second, the SHA256:… fingerprint the first call returned, after you checked it against the machine.                                         |
| `template`                               | string  | Bootstrap template uuid or slug. Omit to use your default.                                                                                                                 |
| `organization`                           | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                          |

### `upgrade-fleet`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.test.connection</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Start — or watch — a staged sweep that brings every behind server up to the current G8Deck node stack. Machines are upgraded ONE AT A TIME and the sweep stops at the first failure, leaving the rest untouched; it is never simultaneous. Only the difference is applied, never a re-bootstrap. Call with dry_run to see the plan without starting anything, and call again while a sweep is running to poll its progress rather than starting a second. ADOPTED servers are excluded and always will be: they carry no G8Deck stack to compare against, so nothing a fleet upgrade installs can reach them — the response names each one. Protected servers (the control plane) and unreachable ones are excluded too, with the reason.

| Parameter      | Type    | Description                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dry_run`      | boolean | Report the plan — which servers would be upgraded and which are excluded and why — without starting anything. |
| `organization` | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                             |

### `patch-fleet`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.test.connection</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Patch one target — php, node, python, nginx, mysql, mariadb, postgresql, redis, valkey, container-runtime or os-security — across the fleet: the packages ALREADY INSTALLED for it are upgraded in place to the newest build the configured repository carries. Never installs anything new and never changes a major/minor version. A CANARY goes first: one server (at least one application, no production application, fewest applications; a canary that proves nothing — nothing-installed or no_applications — hands the role to the next server with an application) is patched and health-checked alone, and the rest are patched in parallel only once it is healthy; canary: false patches every server at once (emergency). A failed canary, or failures on two servers, HALTS the run: status halted with halted_reason, and the servers not reached report skipped (reason halted). After the patch every running application on the server is probed on its health_path through nginx with its domain; a red probe is outcome failed_health, and an application that could not be probed (no health_path, no domain, no HTTP client) is health could_not_probe — neither healthy nor failed — unless its systemd units are down after the patch, which is failed_health. A canary in could_not_probe still fans out, and the run reports canary_unverified: true with canary_unverified_reason naming the missing probe. php reloads each application's php-fpm master gracefully, restarts its queue/Horizon/scheduler workers still on the old binary, and nginx reloads by default; database, cache, container-runtime, node and python restarts are DISRUPTIVE and happen only with restart: true — otherwise the result is restart_pending and the old build keeps running. Each server's result carries the upstream versions (before/after) and the distribution package versions (packages_before/packages_after) — already-current means no package moved because the repository has nothing newer — plus any process still running the replaced binary (stale). Adopted, protected and unreachable servers are excluded with the reason. The control plane is excluded unless include_control_plane: true, which admits ONLY the control plane's own node (never another adopted or protected server); there its Horizon/queue/worker units are never restarted (they run the patch) and report restart_pending. dry_run returns the plan, the canary it would pick and the last run for that target; calling again while a run is active polls it. organization: "*" is the platform emergency, superadmin only: one run per organisation (each audited on that organisation's trail), dry_run reports counts per organisation.

| Parameter                                  | Type            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target` <span class="req">required</span> | string          | What to patch. os-security applies the distribution's security updates only. One of: `php`, `node`, `python`, `nginx`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `postgresql`, `redis`, `valkey`, `container-runtime`, `os-security`.                                                                                                                                                |
| `dry_run`                                  | boolean         | Report which servers would be patched and which are excluded, plus the last run for this target, without starting anything.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `restart`                                  | boolean         | Also restart what still runs the replaced binary for DISRUPTIVE targets (databases, caches, container runtime, node, python, php CLI workers). Default false: those report restart_pending. php-fpm and nginx reload gracefully either way.                                                                                                                    |
| `include_control_plane`                    | boolean         | Also patch the control plane's own server (G8Deck owns its packages). Admits that one server only — other adopted or protected servers stay excluded. Default false.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `canary`                                   | boolean         | Patch one canary server first (at least one application, no production application, fewest applications; a canary that proves nothing — nothing-installed or no_applications — hands the role to the next server with an application) and fan out only once it is healthy. Default true. false patches every server at once — for an operator's emergency run. |
| `nodes`                                    | array of string | Optional server uuids to restrict the run to. Still subject to every exclusion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `organization`                             | string          | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. "*" (superadmin only) is the platform emergency: one run per organisation, each audited on its own trail.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### `restart-pending`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.test.connection</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Act on servers a patch left restart_pending: patched, but a process still runs the old build until restarted (databases, caches, node/python apps without restart: true, or what a graceful step could not move). With no nodes: lists every restart_pending server — the units still on the old build (units), the stale processes, the control plane's held worker units (held, never restarted by G8Deck: they run G8Deck itself, G303), the expected interruption, and any scheduled or running restart. With nodes: restarts EXACTLY the units the patch recorded as pending on those servers, now — the patch's own restart step limited to those units, with the same before/after health check — and records the outcome on the run result (restarted, failed_health or failed) with an audit row naming you as the approver. schedule: true queues it for the organisation's next maintenance window instead (the scheduler restarts it there); cancel: true cancels a scheduled one. target narrows to one patch target when a server is pending for several. Refused while a patch run is active for the organisation. Same permission as patch-fleet: organisation administrator.

| Parameter      | Type            | Description                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nodes`        | array of string | Server uuids to act on. Omit to list every restart_pending server without acting.                                                                                     |
| `target`       | string          | Only results of this patch target. One of: `php`, `node`, `python`, `nginx`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `postgresql`, `redis`, `valkey`, `container-runtime`, `os-security`. |
| `schedule`     | boolean         | Queue the restart for the organisation's next maintenance window instead of now. Default false.                                                                       |
| `cancel`       | boolean         | Cancel a scheduled restart on these servers. Default false.                                                                                                           |
| `organization` | string          | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                     |

### `set-patch-policy`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.test.connection</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Change the organisation's patch policy. Takes final values for the fields you pass; omitted fields keep theirs. mode: automatic (default, recommended) / notify_only / manual — moving to a LESS automatic mode, or setting a server override to notify_only or manual, is refused unless acknowledge_risk: true, and the acknowledgement is audited (who, when, which mode). notify_only and manual leave servers unpatched until someone acts. Window: window_days (ISO weekdays 1=Monday…7=Sunday), window_start / window_end (HH:MM; an end before the start wraps midnight), timezone (IANA, e.g. Asia/Kuala_Lumpur). allow_disruptive_restarts lets a scheduled run restart databases, caches, node/python apps inside the window (otherwise restart_pending). critical_outside_window lets a critical advisory patch outside the window (graceful only). contact_emails and webhook_url are extra contacts for patch notices; the webhook URL is stored encrypted and never returned. node + node_override sets one server's override: inherit, or a mode no more automatic than the organisation's. Returns the policy as get-patch-policy does.

| Parameter                   | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mode`                      | string           | automatic (default) patches inside the window; notify_only and manual never patch and need acknowledge_risk: true.                                         |
| `scope`                     | string           | security (default) or all. One of: `security`, `all`.                                                                                                      |
| `window_days`               | array of integer | ISO weekdays the window opens on: 1=Monday … 7=Sunday. Default every day.                                                                                  |
| `window_start`              | string           | HH:MM, in timezone. Default 02:00.                                                                                                                         |
| `window_end`                | string           | HH:MM, in timezone. Default 05:00. Earlier than window_start wraps midnight.                                                                               |
| `timezone`                  | string           | IANA timezone. Default Asia/Kuala_Lumpur.                                                                                                                  |
| `allow_disruptive_restarts` | boolean          | Let scheduled runs restart databases, caches, container runtime, node and python inside the window. Default false: restart_pending.                        |
| `critical_outside_window`   | boolean          | Let a critical advisory patch outside the window, graceful restarts only. Default true.                                                                    |
| `contact_emails`            | array of string  | Extra addresses for patch notices, beyond the organisation's owners and administrators.                                                                    |
| `webhook_url`               | string           | https URL for patch notices. Stored encrypted, never returned. Pass null to clear.                                                                         |
| `node`                      | string           | A server uuid whose override to set, with node_override.                                                                                                   |
| `node_override`             | string           | inherit, or a mode no more automatic than the organisation's. One of: `inherit`, or another value the server accepts.                                      |
| `acknowledge_risk`          | boolean          | Required (true) when moving the organisation or a server to notify_only or manual: you accept that its servers stay unpatched until someone acts. Audited. |
| `organization`              | string           | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                          |

### `publish-advisory`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>mcp.access.cross-tenant</code></p>

Publish a security advisory for one patch target (php, nginx, node, …) and tell every organisation it reaches. Each managed server is matched from the versions its patch runs RECORDED (patch-fleet result `after`) against `ranges` — one entry per branch: {branch: "8.4", fixed: "8.4.27"} (fixed omitted or null = no fixed build yet, every version on that branch exposed; introduced = lower bound; component = substring the probe line must contain). States: exposed, fixed (at/after the fix, outside the range, or not installed), not_exploitable_here (set later with assess-advisory) and unknown (no recorded version, or a branch no range covers — never reported as fixed). Organisations with an exposed server are told by email, in-app and their policy webhook (signed), worded by their patch policy: automatic → "will be patched in your window at HH:MM <tz>" with Patch now / Postpone 24h; notify_only/manual → "Action needed". CRITICAL (CVSS ≥ 9 or actively_exploited — anything lower is refused for those) in an automatic organisation with critical_outside_window starts a patch run NOW, outside the window, graceful restarts only, on the exposed servers the scheduler can reach (never adopted servers or the control plane), and sends "Done: before → after, health" when it settles. dry_run: true reports each organisation's exposure without saving or telling anyone. Ops only (mcp.access.cross-tenant).

| Parameter                                       | Type            | Description                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target` <span class="req">required</span>      | string          | The patch target the advisory is about. One of: `php`, `node`, `python`, `nginx`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `postgresql`, `redis`, `valkey`, `container-runtime`, `os-security`. |
| `title` <span class="req">required</span>       | string          | Short title, e.g. "nginx alias/AIO/SSI".                                                                                                                                   |
| `cves` <span class="req">required</span>        | array of string | CVE ids, e.g. ["CVE-2026-15176"].                                                                                                                                          |
| `severity` <span class="req">required</span>    | string          | critical = CVSS ≥ 9 or actively exploited. One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`.                                                                                    |
| `cvss`                                          | number          | CVSS score, 0–10.                                                                                                                                                          |
| `actively_exploited`                            | boolean         | Known exploitation in the wild. Forces critical.                                                                                                                           |
| `ranges`                                        | array of object | —                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `branch` <span class="req">required</span>      | string          | —                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `introduced`                                    | string          | —                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `fixed`                                         | string          | —                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `component` <span class="req">required</span>   | string          | One entry per branch: branch prefix, optional introduced (lower bound), fixed (omit = no fix yet), component (probe-line substring).                                       |
| `condition`                                     | string          | Exploitable only when … (e.g. "alias with rewrite, aio, or ssi on").                                                                                                       |
| `source_urls` <span class="req">required</span> | array of string | https source URLs (vendor advisory, CSA, distro tracker).                                                                                                                  |
| `published_at`                                  | string          | ISO 8601; defaults to now. The SLA clock starts here.                                                                                                                      |
| `dry_run`                                       | boolean         | Report exposure per organisation without saving or notifying.                                                                                                              |

### `assess-advisory`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>mcp.access.cross-tenant</code></p>

Record that an advisory's condition is ABSENT for one organisation — its servers are in the affected range but not exploitable there (e.g. nginx: the generated config uses no alias with rewrite, no aio, no ssi). Servers that would read exposed then read not_exploitable_here: mitigated, not fixed, still listed, and a later patch still moves them to fixed. The reason is required (it is the compliance evidence) and the assessment is audited with your name. withdraw: true removes it. Ops only (mcp.access.cross-tenant).

| Parameter                                        | Type    | Description                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `advisory` <span class="req">required</span>     | string  | Advisory uuid.                                                                        |
| `organization` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Organisation uuid or slug.                                                            |
| `reason`                                         | string  | Why the condition is absent there (required unless withdraw). At least 10 characters. |
| `withdraw`                                       | boolean | Remove the assessment; exposed servers read exposed again.                            |

### `create-git-credential`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>git-credentials.create.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Store an access token G8Deck clones HTTPS repositories on one git host with — the Git Credentials page's action and rules. The token travels INBOUND ONLY: it is encrypted at rest and never returned, by this tool or any other. Without a token it is a bookkeeping entry (and optionally a pinned SSH host key); repositories on that host keep cloning anonymously. One credential per host per organisation. SSH repository URLs do not use this: they authenticate with a per-application deploy key G8Deck generates when the application is created, and only its PUBLIC half is ever shown. Requires being an owner or administrator of the organisation.

| Parameter                                | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Unique in the organisation, 2–120 characters.                                                                                                                                    |
| `host` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | Git host, e.g. github.com or git.example.com:8443. A URL is reduced to its host. One credential per host.                                                                        |
| `token`                                  | string  | Personal access token with read-only repository access. Inbound only — never returned.                                                                                           |
| `username`                               | string  | Username to pair with the token. Most providers accept any non-empty value.                                                                                                      |
| `host_key`                               | string  | The host's SSH public key line(s) to pin ("&lt;type&gt; &lt;base64&gt; [comment]" per line, as ssh-keyscan prints). Omit for hosts G8Deck already pins (github.com and friends). |
| `description`                            | string  | Optional, up to 255 characters.                                                                                                                                                  |
| `is_active`                              | boolean | Default true.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `organization`                           | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                                |

## Destructive tools

Each needs a token carrying `mcp:destroy`, and most also need an identifying value retyped into a confirmation argument. A mismatch is refused and audited.

### `delete-infra-provider`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.delete.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Delete an infrastructure provider row. This destroys no machine: it removes G8Deck's credential for one, so an adopted host becomes unreachable rather than gone — the VM keeps running and keeps billing until its own owner deletes it. Refused for the control plane, and while live deployments, node pools, managed nodes or bootstrap history still point at it. Requires the provider name retyped exactly in confirm_name, and a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                        | Type   | Description                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider` <span class="req">required</span>     | string | Provider uuid.                                                            |
| `confirm_name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The provider's exact name, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                   | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.         |

### `retire-managed-node`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>infra-providers.delete.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Delete a managed server from G8Deck (the tool keeps its name; the act is what the UI now calls Delete). By default it uninstalls nothing and shuts nothing down: the server keeps running and keeps billing, G8Deck simply stops counting it. Pass destroy_machine=true to ALSO delete the machine at the cloud account it was created through — irreversible, its data goes with it, and it is accepted only for a machine G8Deck itself created (an adopted machine is refused, because G8Deck was never what made it exist). Pass remove_connection=true when this is the provider's last live machine and it is already gone for good (for example: destroyed at the vendor outside G8Deck) — its provider row is released too rather than left behind reaching nothing; refused for an adopted provider, whose credential is the operator's own. Bootstrap history is kept either way. Refused for the control plane. Confirmation is the node's SSH HOST address, not its hostname — a hostname can be blank or duplicated, an address is the thing an operator actually read. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                        | Type    | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `node` <span class="req">required</span>         | string  | Managed node uuid, from list-managed-nodes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `confirm_host` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | The node's exact SSH host address, retyped — not its hostname, which may be blank or shared. Anything else is refused and audited.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `destroy_machine`                                | boolean | Also DELETE the machine at the cloud account it was created through. Irreversible and its data goes with it. Defaults to false, which touches nothing. Refused for a machine G8Deck did not create — delete an adopted machine at its own hosting provider.                                                             |
| `remove_connection`                              | boolean | Also remove the infra provider row, when this is its last live machine and nothing else depends on it. Defaults to false. Refused for an adopted provider (its credential belongs to the operator) and for one another live machine or node pool still reaches through — check with get-infra-provider first if unsure. |
| `organization`                                   | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

### `drop-managed-database`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>database-servers.manage.databases</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Drop a database on a managed server. This DELETES THE DATA and cannot be undone — there is no snapshot taken here and no undo; take a backup first if the data matters. The drop is queued and the record is soft-deleted only after the daemon accepts it, so a record that is still present means the daemon has not dropped it yet. The name stays reserved on that server afterwards. Confirmation is the database NAME, which is unique on the server you just named. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Database server uuid, from list-database-servers.                                                                 |
| `managed_database` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Managed database uuid, from list-managed-databases.                                                               |
| `confirm_name` <span class="req">required</span>     | string | The database's exact name, retyped. It is unique on the server named above. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                       | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                 |

### `drop-database-user`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>database-servers.manage.users</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Drop a login role on a managed database server. It deletes no data — the databases and their contents are untouched — but anything still connecting as this role stops being able to, which on a deployed application is an outage that arrives at its next connection rather than now. Check list-managed-databases for what this role holds first. The drop is queued and the record is soft-deleted only after the daemon accepts it; the username stays reserved on that server afterwards. Confirmation is the USERNAME, which is unique on the server you just named. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Database server uuid, from list-database-servers.                                                                 |
| `database_user` <span class="req">required</span>    | string | Database user uuid, from list-managed-databases.                                                                  |
| `confirm_username` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The role's exact username, retyped. It is unique on the server named above. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                       | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                 |

### `withdraw-database-server`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>database-servers.delete.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Remove a database server RECORD from G8Deck. It uninstalls nothing and drops nothing: the daemon keeps running, its databases and users are untouched on disk, and the machine underneath keeps billing — a database server is a daemon on a managed node, and the node is what a hosting provider charges for. Use retire-managed-node with destroy_machine=true to stop that. What does go is G8Deck's stored admin credential, because G8Deck stops administering it. The record is soft-deleted. Confirmation is the server's ENDPOINT (host:port) as list-database-servers reports it, not the engine name — every PostgreSQL server is called PostgreSQL. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                            | Type   | Description                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Database server uuid, from list-database-servers.                                                                                         |
| `confirm_endpoint` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The server's exact endpoint as host:port, retyped — not the engine name, which repeats across rows. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                       | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                                                                         |

### `promote-database-replica`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>database-servers.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Manual failover: promote a PostgreSQL replica to its cluster's primary. DESTRUCTIVE to the old primary: it is stopped and disabled first (so it cannot keep taking writes), then needs a rebuild; every other replica is marked for rebuild too. If the old primary cannot be stopped, the promotion stops and changes nothing — unless accept_data_loss is true (the "primary is dead" case), which continues and records it unfenced. Refused, with the reason, when the replica has no fresh healthy probe, its replication could not be read, or it is not a standby. Refused when the last probe shows a risk of losing writes (not receiving, lagging, lag unknown, or the primary not healthy) unless accept_data_loss is true — replication is asynchronous, so anything the replica never received is lost. Afterwards managed databases and users move to the new primary and attached applications get the new DB_HOST/DB_URL through the attach path — effective on each application's NEXT DEPLOY. Queued; read the outcome with get-database-cluster. Confirmation is the replica's endpoint (host:port). Requires mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                            | Type    | Description                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database_server` <span class="req">required</span>  | string  | The replica's database server uuid, from get-database-cluster.                            |
| `confirm_endpoint` <span class="req">required</span> | string  | The replica's exact endpoint as host:port, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `accept_data_loss`                                   | boolean | Promote even when writes may be lost or the old primary cannot be stopped. Default false. |
| `organization`                                       | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                         |

### `remove-storage-member`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>storage-servers.update.item</code> · organisation owner or administrator only</p>

Take one additional node out of a managed storage server's Garage cluster: a layout change, after which Garage moves that node's copies onto the remaining nodes. REFUSED when it would leave fewer nodes than the replication factor. The primary node cannot be removed (delete the storage server for that). It stops and uninstalls nothing: the daemon on the removed machine keeps running with its data directory and the cluster secret, and the machine keeps billing. Confirmation is the member machine's SSH host address as get-storage-cluster reports the member, retyped. Requires a token carrying mcp:destroy.

| Parameter                                          | Type   | Description                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `storage_server` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Storage server uuid.                                                                  |
| `member` <span class="req">required</span>         | string | Member uuid, from get-storage-cluster.                                                |
| `confirm_host` <span class="req">required</span>   | string | The member machine's SSH host address, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                     | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.                     |
